goalbuddy_receipt_v1.rationale: The deterministic policy, additive stores, TTL exclusion, legacy defaults, and Hindsight metadata are materially implemented, and the Codex verifier failure is solely a broken PATH entry. Governance is not milestone-ready: the claimed calibration is a 24-case synthetic holdout dominated by 20 near-identical positives, with no separate calibration split; its metric aborts on misclassification instead of measuring errors. The product review API also accepts caller-supplied verifier signals, and the release canary still proves manual approval. These are security and oracle gaps, so storage work must wait for one bounded governance-repair package.

worker_package.objective: Close the Lot 0 governance milestone without starting Working Memory or graph work. Replace the self-confirming admission corpus with separate versioned calibration and holdout sets containing diverse positive, negative, TTL, restricted, conflict, scope, ontology, duplicate, fragment, verifier-outage, and high-impact cases; make measurement return a confusion report without aborting on mismatches, record the calibrated threshold profile, and require >=95% holdout auto-activation precision plus <5% standard-claim human exceptions. Strengthen admission verification so the deterministic admission ID is recomputed and every store binds the attestation to the expected candidate, workspace, policy version, evidence-bearing candidate, and TTL semantics. Remove the HTTP trust boundary violation: automatic-mode review/re-evaluation must use only the server-configured verifier, never `verification` supplied in a request body; forged client signals must remain non-recallable. Change the sacrificial Codex canary and release evidence to prove automatic admission with an independent deterministic verifier and no `reviewCandidate` call. Recover the current verifier environment by resolving and validating an explicit Codex executable, all PATH candidates, and the packaged ChatGPT Codex fallback before running the canary, then pass the absolute executable through. Make the default full test suite classify unavailable local Hindsight runtime as unavailable/skipped evidence rather than fail, while retaining strict assertions when it is present. Preserve flags-off legacy behavior and all existing user changes.

stop_if: Calibration and holdout labels are not independent splits, are dominated by repeated identical signal vectors, or cannot truthfully measure false positives and human-exception rate.
Any client-provided HTTP field can still impersonate the configured independent verifier or directly cause activation.
The release canary still calls `reviewCandidate`, uses legacy-manual mode, or reports success without an independently verified admission attestation.
Admission artifacts cannot be bound to candidate ID, workspace ID, policy version, evidence, and deterministic admission ID without rewriting existing immutable legacy artifacts.
Flags-off/default legacy behavior or byte-preserved v1/v2 compatibility would change.
Verifier recovery would install, replace, or mutate the host Codex installation instead of selecting a validated existing executable.
Tests require a live Hindsight, Ollama, Graphiti, Neo4j, real vault, credentials, or network write; unavailable live infrastructure must be explicit rather than silently passed.
A required change falls outside allowed_files or enters Working Memory, graph, ontology, MCP recall, deploy, or production rollout.
The same verification failure remains unresolved after two attempts.

findings: `memory-admission-policy.mjs:154-198` makes the final four-way decision deterministically from verifier signals; candidate confidence is not read by the decision function.
`memory-admission-policy.mjs:156-163` leaves missing verification pending and rejects a verifier sharing extractor model and prompt identity.
`codex-workspace-store.mjs:382-469` and `product-store.mjs:701-809` persist immutable admission artifacts, activate only auto/TTL decisions, and make admission replay idempotent.
Both stores exclude expired TTL memory from normal recall; quarantine, discard, and pending verification do not create recallable memory.
Default store, compiler, app, and CLI modes remain `legacy_manual`; existing legacy tests pass and product v1 bytes remain unchanged.
The claimed holdout contains only 24 cases: 20 auto-activate, one TTL, two discard, and one quarantine; all 24 are standard sensitivity.
The 20 positive cases repeat essentially the same high signal vector, so 100% precision and 4.17% exceptions are construction artifacts, not credible calibration evidence.
No separate calibration dataset exists even though the blueprint requires calibration on a set separate from final testing.

`measureAdmissionCorpus` throws on the first expected/actual mismatch at line 235, so it cannot produce a confusion report for an imperfect policy; reported precision can only come from a fully pre-matched fixture.
Thresholds remain hard-coded defaults rather than a recorded result tied to a calibration split.
`supermemory-app.mjs:334-338` passes the request body directly to `product-store.reviewCandidate`.

`product-store.mjs:1325-1348` accepts `verification` from that body and feeds it to `admitCandidate`; a local API caller can therefore self-assert `independent:true` and submit policy signals for a quarantined claim.
Normal ingest correctly uses the server-configured verifier at `product-store.mjs:1127-1143`; exception re-evaluation must use the same trusted boundary.
`product-hindsight.mjs:59-81` carries legacy/admitted status, admission ID, decision, policy version, TTL, source, snapshot, interpretation, and workspace metadata.
`verify-m1-hindsight-promotion-recall-fixture.mjs:114-158` rejects admitted projection payloads missing admission ID, allowed decision, or policy version.
Focused Hindsight metadata tests pass; no regression was found at this boundary.
`run-codex-integration-canary.mjs:336-368` still constructs legacy governance and calls `reviewCandidate(action=approve)`.
The release evidence therefore remains a nominal manual-review oracle even though separate focused tests exercise automatic admission.
The release canary must demonstrate candidate creation → independent verification → deterministic admission → projection → cited recall without a review call.
`/opt/homebrew/bin/codex` resolves to the npm shim whose packaged arm64 binary is missing and fails with ENOENT.
`/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex --version` succeeds as `codex-cli 0.146.0-alpha.9.2`.

With the ChatGPT resource directory prepended to PATH, `npm run verify:codex` passes all nine checks, including oracle_canary and codex_cli. The T002 verifier blocker is therefore environmental, not a governance-code failure.
The 30 focused tests and all three normative verifiers reported by T002 pass.
`npm run verify` passes completely.
`npm run verify:release` passes.
`git diff --check` passes.

`npm test` runs 151 tests with 150 passing; only `tests/hindsight-local-runtime-unblock.test.mjs` fails because it requires a currently healthy live localhost Hindsight service. This is an existing environment-coupled test, not a T002 regression, but it prevents full-suite proof.
T002-reported changed files stay within its approved allowed_files.
The repository remains heavily dirty with unrelated tracked and untracked user work; no reset, staging, installation, or source mutation was performed by this Judge.
Fresh structural index evidence was supplied for project `SuperMemory`: 7,823 nodes, 12,489 edges, skipped_count=0, persistence=false; deploy remains excluded and is not assessed here.
Working Set, Evidence Ledger, projection lifecycle, graph, ontology, router/MCP, and deploy remain deferred.
Because admission calibration, verifier trust, and the release oracle are not yet trustworthy, existing T004 must not begin storage/evidence implementation.
